in_arabic.name: بَرَاء
in_arabic.meaning: بَرَاء يعني منزه عن السوء و المعاصي و الذنوب
in_arabic.long_meaning: بَرَاء هو اسم علم مذكر من أصل عربي و معناه منزه عن السوء و المعاصي و الذنوب، خالي من الشر و الإثم. ورد ذكره في القرآن الكريم في سورة آل عمران: وَمَا كَانَ لِنَبِيٍ أَنْ يَأْخُذَ أَخًا بَيْنَ الأَنْبِيَاءِ وَلَكِنِ الَّذِي يَأْخُذُ أَخًا مِنْ قَوْمِهِ بَرَاءُ النَّبِيُّ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ

in_urdu.name: برا
in_urdu.meaning: برا مطلب ہے بری باتوں سے پاک، نیک، اچھا
in_urdu.long_meaning: برا ایک مذکر اسم ہے جو عربی زبان سے نکلا ہے۔ اس کا مطلب ہے وہ شخص جو بری باتوں سے پاک ہے، نیک اور اچھا ہے۔ یہ نام جنوبی ایشیائی مسلمانوں میں خاص طور پر اردوگوพูด人々 میں مقبول ہے۔ اس نام کی اصیل عربی جڑیں ہیں اور اسلامی تقالید میں اس کا بڑا دینی اور ثقافتی اہمیت ہے۔

in_hindi.name: बरा
in_hindi.meaning: बरा का अर्थ है बुराई से मुक्त, अच्छा और नेक
in_hindi.long_meaning: बरा एक पुल्लिंग नाम है जो अरबी भाषा से आया है। इसका अर्थ है वह व्यक्ति जो बुराई से मुक्त है, अच्छा और नेक है। यह नाम भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में प्रचलित है और इसका उच्चारण बरा है। इस नाम का महत्व इस्लामी परंपरा में बहुत अधिक है और यह नाम अरबी मूल का है।

in_pashto.name: براء
in_pashto.meaning: براء د بری خبرو څخه پاک معنی لري
in_pashto.long_meaning: براء یو مذکر نوم دی چی د عربي ژبې څخه يی اخیستل شوی دی. دغه نوم د بری خبرو څخه د پاکۍ معنا لري، نیک او ښه کس. دا نوم په افغان او پښتون دود کې ډیر مشهور دی او د پښتو تلفظ یی براء دی.

data.cultural_impact: The name Bara, which originates from the Arabic language and means 'rain, thunder', holds a notable place in Muslim culture as it is the name of various historical figures and cities. One of the most renowned scholars by the name of Imaam Baraa' Ibn Aasim Al-Azdi is mentioned in Hadith as an example of the Sahabah (Companions of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ) who were passionate about the establishment of the Islamic State and the implementation of Shari'ah law. This shows how the Arabic name Bara, with its association to the power and vastness of the sky and rain, can symbolize strength, renewal, and the enduring spirit of the Muslim community.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Bara holds spiritual significance as it is mentioned in Surah Al-An'am (6:97) where Allah Almighty says, "Thus We have sent you (O Muhammad) with the truth and verily, there came to you the truth (the Quran) and a faithful belief; and asking for their Lord's forgiveness, [they were]euoned only by their Lord. And Jeddah was indebted [to her people] in favor of her Lord and was a source of security for the three settled villages thereunder; and thereon there are [houses] ofiac dread: for such indeed in their Lord's sight is an honor, and it was promised to them in the worldly life that they would be immune from the torment of the people." Here, the mention of the name Bara is connected to Allah's promise of protection for the believers. In Surah Al-Mumtahanah (60:8), Allah says, "Allah propounds to you an example from those before you: the people of the City [referring to Nuh and his people]. They belied the Messengers and asked for something other than what Allah had ordained for them. So We rained upon them a rain [of torment] from the sky, because of their persistence in contradiction. And We made their clinched armies a population of jinn and mankind they had no power over but a quivering [terror] in their hearts. That is because they [rejected] the signs of Allah and Allah is Severe in penalty." This passage refers to the destructive rain sent by Allah upon those who rejected Him, which further illustrates the importance of the Arabic root 'br' (rain, thunder) in Islamic belief.
